c: Infinite Corridor fires a white beam around the player in twelve directions clockwise one at a time. The beam does no damage, but will freeze any enemy it hits. After the freezing beam has completed one full rotation and it fires upwards in the 12 o'clock direction, it creates a spinning, shining rainbow aura around the player, halving the health of every enemy on screen.
Infinite Corridor can attack and defeat the otherwise intangible
before minute 30, causing them to drop

With Limit Break, Infinite Corridor can be further leveled up.

The freezing beam travels around the player like a clock, shooting out at "12 o'clock," then at "1 o'clock," and so on. This means the freezing beam only has 12 directions it can fire. This also makes the freezing beam very predictable.
It is possible to keep freezing the same enemy multiple times. This is especially useful for bosses and
Frozen enemies cannot damage the player, so it is safe to touch them.

as stronger enemies start coming in.
Infinite Corridor's health halving effect works on the Reaper, making quick work to lower their health to an amount that is viable to be killed by any character when combined with the
In fact, using this weapon against the Reaper is one of the only ways for it to drop
White Hand), the other being the use of the Crimson Shroud.

While using both weapons is ideal, you can kill the Reaper using Infinite Corridor alone without its counterpart, although this means any hit from the Reaper can still be fatal if one fails to consistently keep freezing it. The mirages from the
can serve as a backup way of keeping the Reaper away from the character.
Infinite Corridor is also the easiest way to defeat
, as it is vulnerable to its health halving effect and it helps counteract its constant healing.
